chunks: “The Mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله during his time was by the minaret that is in the middle of the mosque, and above it toward the qiblah, about thirty cubits, and to its right, to its left, and behind it, about the same. So seek out that place, and if you are able for your place of prayer to be in it, then do so, for one thousand prophets prayed in it. It was only called al-Khayf because it is elevated above the valley, and whatever rises above it is called khayf.”

key_terms.أَلْفُ نَبِيٍّ: one thousand prophets, indicating the site's sanctity
key_terms.الْخَيْفَ: the name of the place, referring to elevated ground above a valley
key_terms.الْمَنَارَةِ: the minaret or marked elevated point used here as a spatial reference
key_terms.الْوَادِي: the valley below which the place is elevated
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ: mosque; the sacred prayer space being described

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of praying in Masjid al-Khayf and why is it called al-Khayf?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the area of Masjid al-Khayf associated with the prayer place of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and encourages praying within that blessed location if possible. It also explains the naming of al-Khayf as a place elevated above the valley and highlights its sanctity by stating that one thousand prophets prayed there.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.690 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (sw) during his time extended near the minaret located at the center of the mosque, and above it towards the Qibla, approximately thirty cubits, as well as a similar distance to its right, left, and behind. So, focus on this area, and if you can make your place of prayer within it, then do so, for one thousand prophets have prayed there. It was called 'al-Khayf' because it is elevated above the valley, and anything that rises above it is called 'Khayf.'"
